tutorial.title: Setting Attributes Dynamically
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to access and change HTML attributes with JavaScript

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
We've seen how to change the text of an HTML element. Let's now learn how to change HTML attributes with JavaScript.

In this example, we're changing the src attribute of the sprite image on each button press.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Once we've accessed an element with JavaScript, we can get its attributes by adding a . followed by the attribute name.

For example, after we've stored an img element inside the el variable, we write el.src to get the sprite path.

Make sure to pick el, followed by ., and finally src.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Most attributes can be accessed this way. Access and display the href attribute of the a element.

Make sure to pick el, followed by ., and finally href.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also update attribute values. When doing so, we have to remember to place values in between quotes. Update the src attribute.

Make sure to pick =, followed by "https://mimo.app/r/kittles.png".

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can even use attributes to change how elements work and behave on a webpage. Change the input element's type attribute to checkbox.

Make sure to pick type, followed by "checkbox".

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
Changing attributes can be very powerful. By adding the link to the stylesheet, we change this game UI's entire look.

Make sure to pick link followed by href and then style, ., css.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we access an element's attribute after we've stored the element inside a variable?

By coding a period followed by the attribute nameBy coding a semicolon followed by the attribute name

By coding a period followed by the attribute name.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the paragraph?

https://mimo.app/r/kittles.pngel.src

Make sure to pick https://mimo.app/r/kittles.png.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code?

a tags have href, not src attributesThe updated value should be in parentheses

a tags have href, not src attributes.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the p tag?

https://mimo.app/r/clawdius.pnghttps://mimo.app/r/cat.png

Make sure to pick https://mimo.app/r/clawdius.png.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
What type value will the input element have after pressing the button?

emailcheckbox

Make sure to pick email.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
After running the code, will this webpage be linked to a stylesheet?

Yes, we're dynamically setting the stylesheet with JavaScript codeNo, because href is empty

Yes, we're dynamically setting the stylesheet with JavaScript code.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the img element's src attribute.

Make sure to pick "img" followed by el and then ., src.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Update the image element's src attribute.

Make sure to type el.src.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Update the input element's type attribute.

Make sure to pick ., followed by type.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use JavaScript to set the input element's type and placeholder attributes.

Make sure to pick el followed by . and then type, el, ., placeholder.

lessons.title: Lesson #17
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use JavaScript to add a stylesheet to this webpage.

Make sure to pick el followed by . and then href, =, "style.css", ;.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's learn how to access CSS styles and change them with JavaScript.

In this example, pressing the button changes the game's background.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
To access an element's styling, we first have to add the style attribute. We can then specify the exact style we want, like .color.

Make sure to pick .style, followed by .color.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we want to change an element's style, we have to make sure we put the value in between quotes.

Make sure to pick " followed by # and then d7465f, ".

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we have properties with multiple words like background-color, we have to turn them into camel case. Here, we'll use backgroundColor.

Make sure to pick background, followed by Color.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Changing the style with JavaScript works no matter if the previous style was set inline or through a stylesheet.

Make sure to pick el followed by . and then style, ., borderRadius.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do we add after .style?

A . followed by a style like colorA . followed by a value like blue

A . followed by a style like color.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code?

teal should be in between quotescolor should be capitalized

teal should be in between quotes.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we write properties that have multiple words?

In camel case, like borderRadiusIn snake case, like border_radius

In camel case, like borderRadius.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
Can we use JavaScript to change an element's style if it was set with a stylesheet?

Yes, JavaScript can be used to change an element's style no matter where the style was originally setNo, we can only change inline styles

Yes, JavaScript can be used to change an element's style no matter where the style was originally set.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Access and display the p element's background color inside the empty div.

Make sure to pick el followed by . and then style, ., backgroundColor.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Change the display value of the first a element to block.

Make sure to pick "block".

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the correct properties to change the background-color and border-radius styles.

Make sure to pick backgroundColor, followed by borderRadius.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Change the image's border style that's set in style.css.

Make sure to pick img.

chapters.title: Get and Set Attributes  with Methods

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
We've seen how we can change HTML attributes. There's also a quicker way to do this with JavaScript methods.

Press the button to see how we access and change the sprite of a player, for example.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
After accessing and storing the player sprite we'll also need the img element's src attribute.

Let's store it in a new constant variable called spriteLink.

Make sure to pick const, followed by spriteLink.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
To get an attribute's value we can use the getAttribute() method. We place the element first, followed by . and getAttribute().

Make sure to pick img, followed by ., and finally getAttribute.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Inside the parentheses, we specify any attribute we want to get. Here, we'll code src inside quotes to get the sprite source.

Make sure to pick "src".

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can confirm we got the value by printing the spriteLink variable in the p of our index.html file. Click the button to display the attribute.

Make sure to pick p followed by . and then innerText, =, spriteLink.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
getAttribute() also works if we want to get all the values of a given attribute, like the multiple style values.

Make sure to type "style".

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
Aside from getting attributes, we can also set or update attributes!

To set an attribute's value we have to use the setAttribute() method.

Make sure to pick setAttribute.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
Similar to getAttribute(), we first have to specify which attribute we want to set inside the parentheses.

Let's set src as the attribute that we want to set.

Make sure to pick "src".

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
After specifying which attribute we want to set inside the parentheses, we have to also specify the value.

Let's set "https://mimo.app/r/kittles.png" as the value of the src attribute of the sprite. This way we'll change the player sprite.

Make sure to pick ,, followed by "https://mimo.app/r/kittles.png".

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do we specify inside the parentheses of setAttribute()?

The attribute we want to change and the new valueThe attribute we want to change

The attribute we want to change and the new value.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
What gets displayed in this case?

color: teal; font-weight: bold;color: teal;

color: teal; font-weight: bold;.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the getAttribute() method.

Make sure to type getAttribute.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the right attribute inside the parentheses.

Make sure to pick "href".

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Store the attribute values in the correct variables.

Make sure to pick "a", followed by "style", and finally "href".

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code?

The attribute and value are in the wrong orderThe comma should be a semicolon

The attribute and value are in the wrong order.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Change the type of the input element to range.

Make sure to pick "type", followed by ,, and finally "range".

lessons.title: Lesson #17
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add a placeholder element and set its value to 1234.

Make sure to pick setAttribute, followed by "placeholder", and finally "1234".
